biggest_catch: This is savings, not income — you only 'make' money if you were going to spend at that store anyway.
catches: Savings only materialize on planned spending; buying cards for stores you don't use is wasted money.
Discounts range 1-30%; deep discounts cluster on less popular brands.
You pay upfront and hold the balance — your cash is locked until you shop.
Digital cards can take up to 24 hours to arrive — don't buy minutes before checkout.
Raise's 1-year money-back guarantee covers inactive/inaccurate cards, but you must report problems.

c2.evidence: Discounts of 5-40%+ documented (TechCrunch quoting Raise CEO); 1-30% typical per giftcardgranny; buyer protection guarantee documented (dollarsprout: 1-year money-back guarantee)

c3.evidence: No buyer membership fee; you pay the listed discounted price only.

c4.evidence: Concrete: discount bands documented; example $100 card at 10% off = $10 saved

eligibility: Anyone 18+; no purchase restrictions beyond standard Raise account
maximize: Only buy cards for spending you've already planned this week — groceries, gas, coffee, a gift you must buy anyway. Stack: Raise frequently issues promo codes that stack on top of the listed discount (documented by giftcardgranny), so check for a code before checkout. Buy the digital version when you need it fast, but purchase the day before you shop since delivery can take up to 24 hours. Check the card balance in the retailer's app the moment it arrives.
notes: Savings route, not income: payout fields represent dollars saved on planned spend (flagged). Discount bands from TechCrunch (quoting Raise CEO: 5-40%+) and Granny (1-30% typical). Repeatable on every planned purchase — this is the most repeatable mechanism in the lane.
payout_quote: People can expect to save anywhere from 5% to 40% or more on everyday purchases across a variety of brands. Discounts typically range from 1% to 30%, depending on the retailer and current availability.

repeatable.cadence: Repeatable on every planned purchase — this is the most repeatable mechanism in the lane, but it only 'makes' money on spending you were going to do anyway.

s2.note: No buyer fees; pay the discounted price only.

s3.note: Digital cards delivered to Raise wallet/app, typically within 24 hours.

s4.note: Concrete discount bands; savings figures example-based on planned spend.

s6.note: 4 steps: find card, buy at discount, receive, spend.

steps: Search Raise for a retailer you already plan to spend at
Pick the listing with the best discount (compare a few)
Check for a Raise promo code to stack on top
Buy the discounted gift card; digital cards land in your Raise wallet
Spend it on the planned purchase and pocket the discount
timing: Digital card delivery typically within 24 hours; savings realized at checkout
who_pays: Nobody pays you — this is savings, not income. The 'payout' is the discount off a purchase you were already going to make.
who_qualifies: Anyone 18+ with a Raise account; no purchase restrictions beyond a standard account.
work_available: Raise's discounted gift-card marketplace is active — cards are listed for sale at 1–30% off face value.
what_gets_accepted: You're the buyer here: pick a listed card at a genuine discount, and Raise's 1-year money-back guarantee covers inactive or inaccurate cards if you report problems.
costs_and_unpaid_time: No buyer fees — you pay only the discounted listed price. Unpaid time goes to searching for the best discount and waiting up to 24 hours for digital card delivery.
when_cash_arrives: No cash ever arrives — it's a discount, not income. You pay less at checkout when you spend the card on planned purchases, and digital cards typically land in your Raise wallet within 24 hours.
